extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/NIH peer reviewers and preclinical vaccine researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Preclinical SBIR research-plan for development, characterization, immunogenicity and efficacy testing of virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines displaying remodeled influenza HA in mouse (and later ferret) models to support Phase II/IND-enabling work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims (construct, produce, evaluate VLPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate remodeled HA expression constructs that remove highly variable immunodominant antigenic sites but preserve conserved subdominant antigenic regions; sub-clone into appropriate plasmids for VLP creation; produce and characterize VLPs displaying remodeled HA; evaluate presence of conserved subdominant antigenic sites on purified VLPs by immuno-precipitation using antibodies that exclusively recognize these sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the project's primary production/characterization objective and frames downstream selection for immunogenicity and efficacy testing (Aim 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate selection for immunogenicity testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Select VLP constructs that show positive Western blot for remodeled HA and reactivity in immune-precipitation (IP) with at least one of two testing antibodies for further evaluation in mice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only constructs demonstrating biochemical evidence of displaying the remodeled conserved epitope(s) (WB + IP) progress to Aim 2 testing in animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunogenicity screening criteria (mouse sera neutralization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess capacity of immunized mouse sera to neutralize a panel of antigenically distinct influenza A virus strains using an in-vitro micro-neutralization assay; VLP vaccines capable of partially or completely neutralizing antigenically distinct viruses (cross-subtype neutralization) will be advanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sera from groups of five BALB/c mice immunized twice, two weeks apart (IM), pooled for testing; use homologous and heterologous viruses across major phylogenetic HA groups; positives compared to inactivated-virus immunized controls and pre-immunization background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficacy endpoints in lethal challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective efficacy evaluated by monitoring clinical symptoms and survival after lethal challenge with at least three antigenically distinct influenza A subtypes; percent survival at 18 days post-challenge is primary outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Body weight and clinical signs monitored daily; animals with >20% weight loss or severe symptoms are euthanized; experimental design example: 45 mice randomized to 3 groups of 15 (VLP vaccine, inactivated-virus control, placebo), two immunizations two weeks apart, challenge with 10 LD50 of test virus.

rubrics_metrics.name: VLP purification and biochemical characterization standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Purify VLPs from culture medium (concentration by tangential filtration, gradient ultracentrifugation; alternative chromatographic methods under development) and assess purity and identity by Western blot, Coomassie blue and silver staining; total protein by Bradford assay; HA content quantified by ELISA using purified rHA5 standard and anti-HA2 antibody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also perform IP assays with two antibodies (one recognizing a conserved stalk fusion-peptide site and a second polyclonal anti-HA2) to confirm presence of conserved broadly neutralizing epitope(s). Expected production yields from non-optimized systems ~50–100 mg/L; move successful constructs to stably transfected CHO/Vero lines for continuous production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antigen design/remodeling criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Remodel HA to delete dominant variable HA1 regions, preserve/reposition disulfide bridges, introduce hinge linkers, or add protease cleavage sites to expose HA2/stalk conserved determinants; preserve conformational determinants in HA2/HA1-HA2 interface to elicit broadly neutralizing antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design guided by computer and structural analysis; multiple alternative constructs (1TA–5TA, 3TA includes 12aa linker, 5TA includes protease sites) to probe different structural conformations and expose conserved epitopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunization regimen and sample handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Immunize groups of mice (e.g., five BALB/c mice for screening; larger groups for efficacy) twice, two weeks apart via intramuscular route without adjuvant in preliminary studies; collect sera three weeks after booster; pool serum samples from animals to ensure sufficient volume for assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-immunization and inactivated-virus immunized sera as negative and positive controls; determine VLP dose based on Aim 2 results prior to challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serological and functional assay battery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use micro-neutralization and ELISA assays to evaluate serum antibody levels; do not perform hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) because VLP-HA-Rem vaccines are designed to block membrane fusion rather than receptor binding; measure neuraminidase inhibition activity; determine IgG subtypes for Th1/Th2 characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recombinant H5 protein or reassortant reference virus used as antigens; pool sera from two mice per group for serology to ensure volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell-mediated immunity assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure IFN-γ production in splenocytes by ELISPOT from five mice per group after re-stimulation with reassortant virus or purified antigen to evaluate effector T-cell magnitude and type of immune stimulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ELISPOT results provide additional mechanistic correlates of protection beyond humoral assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mucosal immunity evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect nasal and bronchial lavage to assess presence of mucosal antibody using the same serological methods (ELISA, neutralization as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides data on mucosal antibody presence which may be important for respiratory virus protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal welfare and procedure standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow institutional IACUC and AVMA guidelines: anesthetize prior to procedures (ketamine/xylazine dosing provided), collect blood by submandibular vein, euthanize by IP sodium pentobarbital with cervical dislocation secondary procedure; euthanasia triggers include rapid labored respiration, prolonged inappetence, fever, ≥20–25% weight loss, CNS disturbances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal housing in accredited facility (AALAS); veterinary oversight for husbandry, anesthesia, analgesia, euthanasia; perform challenge experiments in BSL-2/BSL-3E certified facilities as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety, containment and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct H5N1 challenge studies in a CDC/APHIS-certified BSL-3E enhanced facility following CDC/NIH BMBL guidance; ensure staff complete required BSL-3 training, security risk assessments, and Select Agent registrations; BSL-2 experiments performed in appropriate BSL-2 facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CHO/Vero cell lines common in biopharma to facilitate regulatory review; plan for IND-enabling studies and Phase II SBIR if promising candidates emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical design and significance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine sample size based on effect size, standard deviation, desired significance (alpha) and power (1−β); set alpha = 0.05 and power = 80% (β = 0.2); use two-tailed unpaired Student's t-test for pairwise comparisons and ANOVA for multiple-group comparisons; consider P < 0.05 as significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior study variability to estimate effect size; analyses performed in Excel for t-tests and ANOVA as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia and humane endpoints in challenge studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Euthanize animals experiencing >20% body weight decrease or severe influenza symptoms (labored breathing, paralysis); record percent survival up to 18 days post-challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humane endpoints minimize animal suffering while preserving statistical integrity of efficacy measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for advancing candidates to further animal models and IND enabling work
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance VLP constructs that demonstrate: (a) biochemical display of remodeled HA (WB and IP), (b) induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies in vitro across homologous and heterologous strains, and (c) protective efficacy in lethal mouse challenge (survival/protection endpoints) to ferret testing and Phase II SBIR/IND-enabling studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider testing combinations with unaltered HA VLPs to detect synergy/competition and evaluate adjuvant or co-administration with standard vaccine if standalone potency insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential problems and alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: If remodeled HAs elicit neutralizing antibodies but not at clinically useful potency, evaluate combination with standard vaccine or test adjuvants; address folding/expression concerns by WB/IP validation and structural/computational redesign with collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan iterative redesign of HA constructs (additional HAs like H3, H7) to broaden subtype coverage; successful approach could be extended to influenza B.
